narrative: The model estimates that you have about a 39 in 100 chance of failing your final year. That is not a certainty, but it is a serious enough risk that the school is requiring remedial courses so you get support before the year ends. The strongest reason behind this warning is your history of one past class failure; students who passed typically had none. Your current record shows zero absences, which is better than the average of about 3.8 absences among students who passed and which worked in your favor, but it was not enough to offset the earlier failure. Your father’s education level being secondary was the third most influential factor and also nudged the prediction toward passing rather than failing, though only modestly; among students who passed, secondary education was common but not the most common level. Overall, the one prior failure was the dominant warning, while your perfect attendance and family background were protective factors. To improve your position, treat the remedial courses as a chance to close gaps, keep attending every class, build a steady weekly study routine, and ask your family and teachers for help early if a subject becomes difficult.
